(PER: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE SACHIN SHANKAR MAGADUM)
Captioned appeal is by claimant for having lost grand son aged 11 years.

Tribunal has awarded a global compensation of Rs.75,000/-
and further, the liability is fastened on the owner of the offending vehicle on the ground that driver did not possess driving licence, as on the date of accident.
NC: 2024:KHC-K:9563 On Negligence:

2. Finding recorded by Tribunal on liability is contrary to law laid down by Hon'ble Apex in the case of PAPPU AND OTHERS Vs. VINOD KUMAR LAMBA AND ANOTHER reported in (2018) 3 SCC 208, and as reiterated by the Full Bench judgment in NEW INDIA ASSURANCE CO. LTD., BIJAPUR vs. YALLAVVA AND ANOTHER, 2020 (2) KCCR 1405 (FB).

entities.text: PAPPU AND OTHERS Vs. VINOD KUMAR LAMBA AND ANOTHER reported in (2018) 3 SCC 208
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: NEW INDIA ASSURANCE CO. LTD., BIJAPUR vs. YALLAVVA AND ANOTHER, 2020 (2) KCCR 1405 (FB)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Judgments cited supra clarify the position on the liability of insurance companies in similar cases.

According to these rulings, the insurance company, despite any concerns regarding the validity of the driver's license, is primarily obligated to fulfill the compensation claim and subsequently has the right to recover this compensation amount from the owner of the offending vehicle.

Based on this legal principle, this Court finds that the insurance company is indeed liable to satisfy the awarded compensation to the claimants, but may,
thereafter, pursue recovery from the vehicle owner.

sentences.text: In the present case, the unfortunate circumstances surrounding the life of the deceased child reveal a deeply saddening story.
The young boy, who had already endured the devastating loss of both his parents, was residing with his maternal grandmother, the appellant in this case.
Despite her personal grief, the appellant took on the role of caregiver and nurtured her grandson, offering him a semblance of stability and familial love.

Tragically, this fragile solace was shattered when the boy lost his life in a road traffic accident on 18.05.2016.
4.
The compensation awarded by the Tribunal in this case, however, does not align with the principles laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Kishan Gopal & Another v. Lala & Others1.

entities.text: Kishan Gopal & Another v. Lala & Others1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In that case, the Hon'ble Supreme Court, by adopting the notional income method, awarded compensation of Rs.4,50,000/- under the head of "Loss of Estate" and an additional Rs.50,000/-
under (2014) 1 SCC 244 NC: 2024:KHC-K:9563 conventional heads.

This precedent establishes a clear framework for determining compensation in cases involving the tragic death of minors,
particularly when their loss impacts the lives of surviving dependents.
5. Guided by the principles articulated in Kishan Gopal (supra), this Court finds that the quantum determined by the Tribunal falls short of the standards set by the Hon'ble Apex Court.
Considering the irreparable loss suffered by the appellant and the tragic circumstances of the case, this Court deems it appropriate to award a global compensation of Rs.5,00,000/-.

This amount, inclusive of Rs.4,50,000/- for loss of estate and Rs.50,000/- under conventional heads, reflects a just and reasonable recognition of the life lost and the impact on the grieving appellant, who had taken on the role of a parent for her late grandson.

6. For the aforesaid reasons, this Court passes the following order:
NC: 2024:KHC-K:9563 ORDER i. Appeal is allowed in part.
ii. Appellant is entitled for enhanced compensation of Rs.4,25,000/- with 6% interest from the date of petition, till realization of entire compensation amount.

iii.
Respondent No.2-Insurance Company shall satisfy the award and recover it from owner of the offending vehicle.
